subject: Clarification: derivative use and feedback permissions in MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Jane Smith <jane.smith@brightwork.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Phillips <mark.phillips@brightwork.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — training & output ownership concerns

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA + order form. Our legal team reviewed and flagged a couple of items we'd like to discuss before we sign: primarily the sections that touch on (1) use of customer data for model training/improvements and (2) ownership/rights in model outputs.

High level concerns:
- Section 5.2 (Feedback/Training License) reads very broad — it would allow Redwood to use any customer-provided content to further train models. We need explicit confirmation that Brightwork data and customer outputs will not be used to create or augment training datasets for models that are commercially available outside of our contract.
- Output ownership language is ambiguous. For outputs generated by Redwood models (e.g., transformed content that our product embeds into customers' UX), we need clarity that Brightwork retains all rights to outputs and any downstream derivatives they create.
- Retention: please confirm maximum retention windows for any cached prompts, KV-cache snapshots, or analytics derived from our content.

I've attached our redline for the MSA; we annotated suggested language (see pg. 3–4). We'd prefer to keep things simple: a narrow feedback license limited to anonymous, aggregated signals used only to monitor and improve service quality — not to train or redistribute models — plus an enterprise opt-out for any training.

Can you route this to your legal team and let us know your baseline? We're trying to close the order form by EOW if possible.

Best,
Jane

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — training & output ownership concerns

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciate the level of detail; I looped in Laura (legal) and Rishi (account lead) so we can get you a consolidated response.

Quick summary of Redwood's baseline and a negotiation path:
- Feedback/Training: Redwood does rely on a limited feedback license to improve service quality. That said, we're open to narrowing the scope. Proposed compromise: a feedback license limited to de-identified, aggregated usage signals and model telemetry (e.g., token-level latency/quality signals, anonymized failure traces) for the purpose of improving our hosted models and runtime. We can explicitly exclude customer-provided files and outputs from being used to create training datasets for general-purpose commercial models.
- Opt-out: we can offer an Order Form add-on ("no-training" option) that prevents Redwood from using any Brightwork content for model training; this would carry an additional fee to offset the operational costs and lost model improvements.
- Output ownership: we typically grant customers rights to use and reproduce outputs for their business, but we avoid assigning proprietary ownership to every generated token. If Brightwork needs an explicit assignment for outputs that are stored and used in your product, we can carve that into the Order Form (with some restrictions related to safety/third-party content).
- Retention: we can commit to a default 30-day retention window for KV/cache and prompt snippets used for debugging, with options to shorten retention or enable automatic deletion for enterprise customers.

Laura — can you take the attached redline and propose concrete language (narrow feedback license + explicit opt-out path + retention/ audit language)? Rishi, can you prepare the pricing delta for the no-training add-on so we can include it in the Order Form?

Jane — we'll come back with a redline from us by early next week. If you have a hard EOW close, we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — training & output ownership concerns

Hi all,

Thanks, Aditya and Jane. I reviewed Brightwork's markup and drafted targeted redlines that reflect the compromise Aditya outlined. High-level changes included in the attached: 

1) Feedback License (Section 5.2) — new language to read: "Provider is granted a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry and usage signals derived from Customer's use of the Services solely to monitor, debug, and improve the Services' performance and reliability. Provider shall not use Customer Content or Output to create or augment training datasets for models that are made generally available for third-party commercial use without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Opt-out / Order Form Add-on — added a clause allowing Customer to select a "No-Training" add-on in the Order Form. When selected, Provider will not use Customer Content or Output (as defined) for any model training, with an agreed pricing uplift.

3) Output Rights — clarified that Customer retains rights to use Outputs produced for their internal and commercial purposes; Provider retains rights to anonymized telemetry and aggregated metrics. We excluded blanket assignment of model IP to Customer while allowing express assignment for specific derivative works by mutual agreement.

4) Retention & Audit — committed to a maximum 30-day retention for transient prompt/KV cache and to provide audit logs for access to Customer Content for a 365-day window upon reasonable request.

Please see the attached redline (MSA_v3_laura_redline.pdf). Jane — the most negotiation points will be around the "create or augment training datasets" prohibition and how granular the opt-out is (full opt-out vs. opt-out for specific model families). If Brightwork wants a full legal guarantee that none of your content will ever influence our model weights globally, that typically maps to an enterprise isolation/Private deployment (VPC) or a contractual no-training commitment plus the add-on.

Let me know which items you'd like us to tighten further.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Laura — thank you for the clear, pragmatic edits. The revised language covers most of our concerns. A couple of outstanding asks from Brightwork's side before we route the order form for signature: 

- We need an explicit clause in the Order Form confirming that Brightwork (and its customers) own the Outputs generated by the Services for use in their products, including any derivatives that Brightwork engineers create from those Outputs. We accept the carve-in for safety/third-party IP, but would like explicit assignment language for downstream productization.
- Please confirm the fee for the No-Training add-on and whether it is pro-rated for our initial 12-month term. Mark — can you also get internal signoff on budget?
- We'd like a DocuSign-ready Order Form with the No-Training add-on prechecked (so procurement can sign faster). If you can send that link to the docusign URL, we can circulate on our side.

If you can provide the finalized redline + the DocuSign link today, we can push this through procurement and aim to sign by Monday. Appreciated — this is time-sensitive for our Q2 launch.

Best regards,
Jane
